designFeedback.findingTitle: Difficulty Signaling via Visual Layering (Bento Grid Weight)
designFeedback.findingDescription: Bento grid is an information architecture decision that controls cognitive load by giving each piece of data its own spatial weight. Apply this to daily todos: bigger/taller cards for high-rank (S/A) tasks, compact rows for routine (C) ones. This mirrors how a hero tile spanning 6 columns creates visual hierarchy through spatial weight so the bigger tile appears more important—letting users visually triage at a glance without text labels.

Karma rewards task completion regardless of task importance, which means the fastest path to a higher score is completing a high volume of small, easy tasks rather than fewer, meaningful ones. Users who discover this optimize for it, and the inbox fills with two-minute items, important projects sit untouched, and the Karma number climbs while actual productivity declines. designFeedback.findingTitle: Immediate Visual Feedback on Task Completion
designFeedback.findingDescription: The core of the experience is the visual feedback loop. When a user marks a habit as complete, the app must acknowledge it—instantly and satisfyingly. This doesn't mean over-the-top fireworks, but a clear, immediate confirmation that their effort has been recorded. Mission Control already does this well with XP pop animations; enhancing it with a color pulse or rank-check notification (e.g., "S-rank locked" at task completion) would deepen the JRPG feel.

Streak forgiveness (freezes, grace days, pause buttons) went from premium feature to baseline expectation, driven by the fact that an unforgiving streak breaks once and then breaks forever, because the psychological cost of restarting from zero is heavier than the cost of skipping today. Mission Control could let players "freeze" one day per week without losing their XP streak, or offer a monthly streak-reset token—keeping the JRPG rank feel while staying psychologically forgiving.

thread-1786428178060-1-streaks-with-conf.title: Streaks with Confetti Micro-Animation on Daily Mark
thread-1786428178060-1-streaks-with-conf.description: Subtle micro animations and visual feedback like confetti explosions reward user actions in real-time. Mission Control has a static streak counter. Add a brief 1-second confetti burst (via CSS keyframes) when a user checks off today's first/final task, triggering only on the streak badge itself. Habit trackers now commonly feature confetti animations and Android support, and retro JRPG menus pair well with particle effects.

thread-1786428178060-2-tap-to-log-quick-.title: Tap-to-Log Quick Action (Finch / Productive Pattern)
thread-1786428178060-2-tap-to-log-quick-.description: Apps like Finch use a cozy, supportive interface for tracking daily goals, making productivity feel gentle rather than demanding. Add a floating "log today" button or a prominent quick-tap region at the bottom of the daily todo list that pre-fills today's date and opens a minimal modal (rank + title only). The best habit tracking apps offer a seamless habits setup process, making sure users log habits fast, reducing friction vs. the current three-step add flow.
